questions.question: Scarcity differs from a shortage because:
options: Scarcity is the PERMANENT condition of insufficient resources; a shortage is a temporary market situation fixable by prices or supply
Shortages are permanent; scarcity is temporary
They are two words for the same thing

questions.question: A millionaire still faces scarcity because:
options: Wants expand with means — and even unlimited money cannot buy unlimited time

questions.question: Scarcity's real force is that it:
options: FORCES RANKING — which want is satisfied first, which waits, which never

questions.question: Bread sold out before noon at the spaza is:
options: A SHORTAGE — temporary, fixed by the delivery van and price adjustment

questions.question: Opportunity cost is defined as:
options: The value of the NEXT BEST alternative sacrificed — not all alternatives forgone
Every alternative given up, added together

questions.question: The R120 calculator whose runner-up was a data bundle has an opportunity cost of:
options: One data bundle — expressed in real terms, not rands
Nothing, since the money was spent anyway

questions.question: The true cost of Thabo's R6 000 machine is:
options: The forgone profit the stock (the next best use) would have earned

questions.question: Every budget debate in a democracy is, properly understood:
options: A fight about tax rates only
An argument about OPPORTUNITY COST — each billion spent is a billion taken from its next-best use

subtopics.title: The Three Questions Every Economy Must Answer

questions.question: The three questions are:
options: WHAT to produce, HOW to produce, FOR WHOM to produce
When, where and why to produce

questions.question: The HOW question carries deep consequences in South Africa because:
options: Labour-intensive methods employ many hands while capital-intensive methods use few — weighty where unemployment is high

questions.question: In a market economy, the three questions are answered by:
options: PRICES — profitable goods get produced, cheapest methods win, output goes to those willing and able to pay

questions.question: South Africa is classified as:
options: A MIXED economy — private markets beside public schools, clinics, grants and state enterprises

questions.question: Economic activity PROMOTES rights when:
options: Employment funds food, shelter, education and dignity — and taxation funds public provision

questions.question: An EXTERNALITY is:
options: A cost paid at the till
A cost landing on third parties that no market price collected — the community breathing the smoke

questions.question: Sustainability means:
options: Producing as much as possible now
Meeting today's needs without robbing tomorrow's

questions.question: The factory-and-river scenario must be answered by:
options: Choosing the side with more marks
Ignoring the pollution if jobs are created
Arguing BOTH sides — employment promoted, health violated — then naming remedies: regulation, taxing the externality, labour-law enforcement

subtopics.title: Not a Shortage — a Forever Thing

questions.question: The test that sorts shortage from scarcity:
options: Can it be fixed by delivery, price or waiting? Shortage. Is it the permanent wanting-more-than-there-is? Scarcity
Does it happen at a spaza?

questions.question: "Get the phone — now you want the earbuds" illustrates:
options: Wants refilling — why the forever-gap never closes

questions.question: The household with R3 000 after rent asks:
options: "What do we want?" — and buys it all
"What comes FIRST?" — scarcity makes life a defended queue of wants

subtopics.title: The Price Tag Behind the Price Tag

questions.question: The "hidden price tag" on every choice reads:
options: What ELSE the money or time would have been — the next-best thing now lived without

questions.question: The Saturday shift earning R150 in exam season carries the hidden tag:
options: "One day of matric revision" — which can cost more than the money earned

questions.question: Even FREE things carry the tag because:
options: The afternoon spent had a next-best use — time is a scarce resource

questions.question: "Money measures the front of the tag; life is lived on the back of it" means:
options: Cash purchases are better than credit
Tags should list alternatives by law
The rand price shows what you PAY; the opportunity cost shows what you GIVE UP — and the second is the true price

subtopics.title: People and the Planet in the Ledger

questions.question: "Rights stop being words on paper" when:
options: The economy works — wages fund school fees, clinic visits and dignity; taxes fund the school's roof

questions.question: "The factory's prices don't include the coughing children" describes:
options: An externality — a cost landing on people who were never part of the deal

questions.question: "Don't feed the family today by burning the table" is the street version of:
options: SUSTAINABILITY — today's needs met without robbing tomorrow's

questions.question: The two-column habit for the factory scenario means:
options: Choosing jobs over health every time
Choosing health over jobs every time
Counting both columns honestly — jobs, incomes, taxes against health, water, tomorrow's resources — then naming the fixes
